A case's `expectations` may declare `ui_flows`, and the harness executes them after the conversation ends, while the workspace is still alive. Each flow is a natural-language step sequence with an `expect` clause ("Open the app. Add a task named 'buy milk'. Reload the page." / "'buy milk' is still visible after the reload."). A host-side agent drives the flow against the delivered app: it reads the page as an ARIA snapshot, decides one action, performs it (`click`, `input`, `keys`, `scroll`, `open`), screenshots, and reads the page back, one box-local exec per step. It addresses elements by ARIA role and accessible name, which survive page changes. It collects rather than judges: a flow is recorded as `completed` when its declared steps were carried out and `incomplete` when the step budget or the flow deadline ran out first, and the agent's closing description of the final page is recorded as evidence, not as a verdict on the `expect`.

Flows run in a headless Chromium inside the box against the app's **forwarded origin** -- `https://<label>.host-<hex>.localhost:8431/`, the URL the client's app tab iframes -- served by a `mngr forward` instance the driver starts for the trial with the same flags minds uses. The flow therefore exercises the product's own serving path (forward proxy, per-host tunnel, label origin, origin-scoped cookies) and needs nothing from the workspace beyond the app it registered; it works against an unmodified workspace template. The flow target is the delivered app that answered its root-path probe; registry order decides only among equally reachable apps.

Each flow gets its own browser (own profile, own CDP port); within a flow, cookies, storage and the open page persist across steps. A flow may declare a `surface`: `origin` (default) is the app's own origin; `minds-ui` (the app as an iframe inside the Minds chrome) is reserved and rejected at generation time until implemented. `script` flows are likewise reserved.

Evidence lands under `verification/flows/<name>/`: a per-step `log.jsonl` (verbatim ARIA snapshot, action, reasoning) and `step_<k>.png` screenshots, plus a manifest entry per flow. Scoring gains a `ui_flows_completed` criterion, registered only for cases that declare flows: it scores the fraction of measurable flows that carried out their declared steps. Whether the app did what a flow's `expect` describes is ruled on once, by the outcome judge, from the step logs and screenshots (a grade-time pre-step flattens them into a digest carrying each flow's declared steps, its `expect`, its completion, the agent's description of the final page, and every step's action, reasoning and page state, and attaches each flow's last four frames, up to 24 in all, saying so in the digest when that ceiling drops any).

A flow that did not get through its declared steps is `failed` and counts against the agent: `step_budget_exhausted`, `flow_deadline`, `no_app_to_open`, and `action_timed_out` -- a page that never offered what a step asked for. Executor failures are `error` with a distinct reason -- `browser_launch_failed`, `cdp_connect_failed`, `forward_unreachable`, `tunnel_down`, `tls_refused`, `step_bridge_failed`, `host_id_unknown`, `unknown_action`, `step_error` -- and are excluded from scoring; an all-errored flow class leaves flows unscored rather than voiding the trial, and reward-details records it under `outcome_evidence`. Which side a step failure lands on is decided by the exception's type, not by its message: a timeout is the app's, anything else out of the executor is the executor's.

The driver and the box-side step script exchange typed models -- `StepRequest`, `StepAction`, `StepResult` in `resources/flow_step_protocol.py`, which both sides import and which is uploaded into the box beside the script. A request the script cannot read fails at the boundary naming the field that broke, and an action kind the script has no branch for is reported as `unknown_action` rather than as anything the app did.

The verification agent's spend is harness spend, reported as `metadata.verifier_agent_usage` beside the decider's. It defaults to the decider model; `--ak verifier_model=...` overrides it. The box image includes Playwright's Chromium (about 300 MB, on the image's last layer); the browser and the step script both run against the box's monorepo venv, so their Playwright versions cannot drift apart.

The workspace template's own `files` app is recognised as a builtin, alongside `system_interface`, `terminal` and `browser`, so it is never counted or probed as a deliverable.
